items.title: MOF warns against fake Threads account using Treasury sec-gen's identity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The public have been advised to beware of a fake Threads account using the name and photograph of Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican. In a Facebook post today, the Finance Ministry (MoF) urged the public not to share personal information or engage with the account. The post also included a screenshot of the fake Threads account bearing Johan's name and photograph.

items.title: Police investigate viral claims of extortion, bribery at Penang roadblock
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Police are investigating a viral social media post alleging that traffic policemen had committed extortion and accepted bribes during a roadblock. Northeast police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said they detected the post today after it drew widespread public attention. Rozak said the investigation would also cover compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and disciplinary aspects involving the personnel concerned.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Sunday, Nov 22, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1583392]] [[nid:1583391]] [[nid:1583390]] [[nid:1583389]] [[nid:1583388]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Fadhlina: Character building must begin at preschool level
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Values education and character building should begin at preschool age to nurture respect and empathy in children. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said quality education was not merely about teaching children to read, write and count, but also about shaping them into individuals with good values and strong character. Fadhlina also expressed her appreciation for the concern and views expressed by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, over increasingly worrying social issues involving the young generation.

items.title: Rough waters no reason to sink the ship, Abang Johari tells GPS members
items.summary: KUCHING:KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) component parties must remain united and not allow differences of opinion to sink the coalition's ship as it navigates the rough waters ahead of the 13th Sarawak state election, says its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg. The Sarawak Premier said differences of opinion were inevitable during an election, but the coalition's component parties must ensure that such differences did not derail their shared goals. He said the entire election machinery must work together to keep the GPS vessel on course, guided by a spirit of camaraderie.

items.title: Sarawak polls: PDP to defend eight seats under GPS banner
items.summary: KUCHING: The Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) aims to defend all eight state legislative assembly seats currently held by the party in the 13th Sarawak state election. Party president Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing expressed confidence that the preparedness of the party machinery, combined with the commitment of the entire PDP leadership and its members, would ensure that all eight seats remain under the party's fold within the Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) coalition. He made these remarks while speaking at the launch of the Gabungan Parti Sarawak election machinery for the 13th Sarawak state election.

items.title: GST should start at 3pct to ease cost of living, says consumer group
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The next government should consider reintroducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) at an initial rate of three per cent to ease the cost of living, says the Kedah Consumers Association (CAKE). Its president, Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff, said the proposed rate would be more reasonable than the previous six per cent, given that prices of essential goods were already high compared with income levels. He said the rising cost of living had put pressure on consumers and businesses, as declining purchasing power led to slower sales.

items.title: Shoes tax break: Cultivating a culture of well-being
items.summary: LETTER: At first glance, the act of including sports shoes in the tax relief list under Budget 2027 might seem like a rather small, even amusing, announcement. Malaysia is facing a growing public health challenge. The Ministry of Health's National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2024: Nutrition found that 30.5 per cent of Malaysian adults were overweight, 23.1 per cent were obese and more than half, or 52.1 per cent, also had abdominal obesity.

items.title: DOSM to conduct household income, expenditure and basic amenities survey next year
items.summary: IPOH: The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) will conduct the 6th Household Income, Expenditure and Basic Amenities Survey (HIES/BA) 2027 from Jan 1 to Dec 31 next year. In a statement, DOSM said the survey aims to collect data on household income, expenditure, and basic amenities to produce official statistics regarding expenditure patterns, poverty rates, cost of living, and income inequality. Meanwhile, DOSM implemented six community development projects worth RM500,000 in Kampung Menderang, Sungkai, through the Kampung Angkat Madani 2026 Programme.

items.title: Flood situation improves in Selangor, Perak as evacuee numbers drop
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Flood situations in Selangor and Perak continued to improve, with the number of evacuees at temporary relief centres declining to 2,151 people from 615 families this afternoon, compared with 2,315 people from 689 families this morning. In SELANGOR , the number dropped to 1,727 people from 484 families, compared with 1,884 people from 532 families recorded this morning. In PERAK , the number of evacuees at five relief centres in four districts also dropped to 424 people from 131 families this afternoon, compared with 479 people from 157 families this morning.

items.title: Seven body bags recovered, 50 missing after Indonesian factory fire
items.summary: One body bag might contain body parts from several people, police said. Authorities said the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable via visual inspection, prompting efforts to collect DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers. "Seven body bags have been recovered," said Wahyu Hidayati, a police disaster victim identification official.

items.title: Death toll from spurious liquor in India's Manipur rises to 16
items.summary: NEW DELHI: The death toll from spurious liquor consumption in India's northeastern state of Manipur has risen to 16, while around 600 people are undergoing treatment in different hospitals, officials said Saturday, reported Xinhua. "The death toll in the spurious liquor incident has risen to 16," a local government official said. The local government of Manipur has constituted a high-level inquiry committee to investigate the incident, identify possible lapses and recommend necessary action.

items.title: Lahore tops the list of most polluted cities in the world
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Hazardous smog turned Pakistan's second-largest city into the most polluted metropolis on the planet on Sunday, leaving authorities helpless to curb pollution, reported German news agency dpa. The air quality in Lahore had a pollutant concentration reading of 289, making it the most-polluted city in the world, according to IQAir, a global environmental think tank. The eastern city bordering India consistently ranked as the world's most polluted major city in the past few weeks since thick and hazardous smog engulfed parts of the central Punjab province.

items.title: Chow rejects Guan Eng's 'unethical' Penang-Perak water deal claims
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow has rebuked Bagan member of parliament Lim Guan Eng for repeatedly alleging unethical conduct in the Perak-Penang bulk water deal. Chow, who chairs PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB) and Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang (PBAPP), said it was regrettable that Lim continued to repeat the allegations despite repeated explanations about the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA). In a statement, Chow questioned why securing 40 years of water supply for residents, industries, investors and future generations could be considered unethical.

items.title: Fahmi allocates RM50k for mass communication students
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has announced a RM50,000 contribution to a coalition of mass communication student clubs to encourage student development programmes. The contribution is aimed at strengthening the coalition and helping students face future challenges, particularly the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on journalism and mass communication, he said. Fahmi also proposed expanding the coalition to all public universities before bringing private universities offering mass communication courses on board.

items.title: Inaccurate descriptions of missing people's journeys could affect insurance claims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Inaccurate descriptions of the journeys of 54 Malaysians still missing after Nepal-Tibet floods could complicate their families' insurance claims, Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) said. MASFIH coordinator and spokesman Dr R. Manivannan said describing the missing Malaysians as participants in climbing activities and expeditions did not reflect the purpose of their journeys and could complicate claims. He said neither group was taking part in climbing or mountaineering expeditions.

items.title: High-income districts may still have struggling households
items.summary: The scale of these pressures is also reflected in KRI's State of Households 2026: From Income to Wellbeing report, which found that Malaysia's median household income stood at RM7,017 a month in 2024. The report found that 46.2 per cent of Malaysian households lived in 22 of the country's 166 districts, where median household income was above the national level. A high median income does not mean every household is well-off.

items.title: Washington governor calls ICE 'out of control' after airport arrests
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The governor of Washington state called US federal immigration agents "out of control" after they arrested two people at Seattle's main airport on Saturday. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers have conducted raids across the United States, part of President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown which has forged ahead despite a rebuke by voters at this month's midterms. ICE later confirmed it had detained two people it said had overstayed their visas.

items.title: Russian cargo ship still on fire off Finland after attack
items.summary: HELSINKI: A fire onboard a Russian cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea continued to burn through the night even as efforts were made to douse the flames, Finland's coast guard said on Sunday. The 16 crew members were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship. The ship, bound for Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, Finland's Defence Forces have said, corroborating an account by Russian officials.

items.title: Red flags put up at four popular beaches in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Red flags have been raised at four beaches in Kelantan due to rough sea conditions during the current Northeast Monsoon. Kelantan Civil Defence Force deputy director Mohd Farid Ishak said the red flags had been raised since Oct 27 to warn the public against entering the water due to strong waves and currents. "Rough sea conditions pose a serious drowning risk, particularly due to strong underwater currents that could pull swimmers out to sea, even when the water surface appears calm," he said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Negri MB Ismail in hospital
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has been hospitalised. His press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, said Ismail was receiving treatment and recovering. On Friday, it was reported that Ismail would remain as Negri Sembilan menteri besar after Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir consented to retain him in the post.

items.title: Reading habits can keep children from excessive screen time - Fahmi
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said without strong reading habits, young people risk spending more time browsing social media platforms such as TikTok rather than exploring quality reading materials that are essential for intellectual development. "Without a good reading foundation and a sustained interest in reading, our children may end up wanting only to spend time on TikTok or lose interest in exploring storybooks. "Reading books not only builds vocabulary but also provides us with a much broader experience," he said at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Lembah Pantai MYReaders programme.

items.title: Fluffy rabbits, dark past draw tourists to Japan island
items.summary: Okunoshima – also known as "Rabbit Island" – has a perimeter of just four kilometres but welcomes thousands of snap-happy visitors attracted by its bunny population each year. "This was my dream," to visit the island, 67-year-old Susan Balzer from Canada told AFP. But the island's cute exterior belies a dark history.

items.title: Amanah wants Gender Parity Act, 30 pct female candidates in polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026 Amanah National Convention today passed a motion calling for the enactment of a Gender Parity Act in political representation to ensure that women make up at least 30 per cent of political candidates in the country. The motion passed with 225 delegates voting aye and 164 nays. Wanita Amanah chief Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu described the passage of the motion as a significant step forward in efforts to strengthen women's representation in the country's democracy.

items.title: Loke: 'Big tent' proposal must first be discussed by PH presidential council
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The "big tent" proposal and other political strategies involving Pakatan Harapan should first be brought to its presidential council for discussion and not aired publicly, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke. Loke also said DAP was open to the proposal for component parties to use their respective party logos in GE16, but this would require further discussions within PH before a final decision was made. On another matter, Loke said the status of his resignation as transport minister on Nov 10 was subject to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's decision.

items.title: Landslide shuts down two lanes, but Cameron Highlands route remains accessible
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: The route to Cameron Highlands remains accessible to motorists, although two of the four lanes along FT185 Jalan Lojing-Gua Musang have been closed following a landslide yesterday. Kelantan Public Works Department (PWD) director Nik Badlihisham Nik Ismail said motorists could still proceed via a diversion route provided at the affected stretch. Yesterday, the left lane at Section 84.15 of federal route FT185 Jalan Lojing-Gua Musang, near Yayasan Albarakah, heading towards Cameron Highlands, had been closed to all vehicles following a landslide .

items.title: Sanusi's daughter discharged from hospital 9 days after motorcycle crash
items.summary: KULIM: Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's daughter, who was injured in a motorcycle crash on Nov 12, was discharged from hospital yesterday. The Kedah menteri besar said his third child was previously treated at the intensive care unit of Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital (HSB) in Alor Star for four days before being transferred to a regular ward. It was reported that Sanusi's daughter suffered injuries to her head and face and broke four fingers and ribs after the motorcycle she was riding crashed.

items.title: Pushers target pupils with 'piu-piu' vapes via social media, delivery services
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Drug trafficking syndicates are increasingly using social media and closed-group applications to market electronic cigarettes (vapes) containing synthetic drugs, locally known as 'piu-piu', with the products delivered to buyers, including students, through courier and delivery services. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the modus operandi allowed transactions to take place without direct contact between sellers and buyers, making it more difficult for the police to detect such activities. Alzafny said police had identified three cases involving secondary school students in the state over the past three years, comprising one case in May and two others early this month.

items.title: DID forecasts flooding in Kelantan districts from Nov 24
items.summary: In Pasir Mas, the areas at risk include Sungai Golok, Sungai Bunut Susu, Sungai Meranti, Sungai Tandak, Sungai Kedotok, Sungai Lanchang, Tasik Garu, Tasik Danau To' Uban, Sungai Rengas, Sungai Lemal and Sungai Lemal Mati. The forecast for Tanah Merah covers Sungai Golok, Sungai Jegor, Sungai Manal, Sungai Jedok, Sungai Air Bujing and Sungai Lanas. In Tumpat, the department identified Sungai Golok, Sungai Pengkalan Nangka, Sungai Mentua, Sungai Gali, Sungai Kelaboran and Sungai Tapang as areas at risk.

items.title: SMS alerts to remain for phones that don't support disaster warning system - Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Smartphone users whose devices do not meet the minimum specifications for the disaster early warning system will not be left out of emergency alerts, as notifications via short message service (SMS) will continue to be available. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the existing notification mechanism operated by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) would continue as usual to ensure all segments of society received timely warnings. Meanwhile, Fahmi said an initial EWS test would be conducted specifically at Parliament tomorrow about 1.30pm.

items.title: No shortcuts, no instant paste: How Banglo289 keeps traditional Malay cuisine authentic at mid-market prices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — In an increasingly competitive food and beverage industry, the use of instant ingredients and commercial pastes has become a common choice among food operators, particularly to save preparation time and reduce costs. However, Banglo289, a restaurant serving traditional Malay cuisine from various states, has chosen to go against the grain by using fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods to preserve the authenticity of its dishes. “The idea behind setting up this restaurant actually stemmed from our observation of a gap in the market for traditional food, particularly Malay cuisine, served in a comfortable setting at reasonable prices.

items.title: Thailand only a transit route for drug syndicates targeting Malaysia, says Kelantan police chief after 700kg meth bust
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 21 — Malaysia-Thailand cross-border security cooperation has continued to strengthen, with authorities in the neighbouring country successfully preventing more than 700 kilogrammes of methamphetamine from entering Malaysia. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the success demonstrated the Thai authorities’ commitment to combating drug smuggling activities that use the country as a transit route before the drugs are brought into Malaysia. Mohd Yusoff said Kelantan police had previously held meetings with the Thai authorities to strengthen security cooperation, particularly in combating drug smuggling and criminal activities along the border of the two countries.

items.title: Four teenagers under 15 arrested after ramming police car during chase on North-South Expressway
items.summary: Tapah district deputy police chief DSP Mohd Fadzil Ismail said a team of officers on patrol duty received information at 4.20 pm yesterday from the Tapah district police headquarters (IPD) control centre to assist officers from the Ringlet police station in tracking down a Toyota Cherry multi-purpose vehicle occupied by several individuals suspected of being involved in a kidnapping case. In an effort to intercept the suspect’s vehicle, the police vehicle’s bumper was hit by the suspect’s vehicle,” he said in a statement today. Mohd Fadzil said another police vehicle from the Ipoh district police headquarters joined in the chase before the suspect’s vehicle was successfully intercepted at Simpang Pulai.

items.title: Don’t push your child into a boarding school if they’re not ready, Fadhlina tells parents as Education Ministry weighs more wardens and counsellors
items.summary: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the aspiration of parents to see their children gain admission to fully residential schools should be balanced with the children’s own abilities and emotional readiness. Our dreams as parents must align with our children’s own abilities and emotional readiness,” she said in a Facebook post today. The discussions covered compliance with standard operating procedures, hostel management, and the importance of parents assessing their children’s level of readiness before sending them to boarding schools.

items.title: Bumiputera firms are listing on Bursa, but Akmal Nasrullah wants them to go bigger
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Five Bumiputera companies successfully listed on Bursa Malaysia between April 2025 and September 2026, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. The companies are Orkim Bhd, which was listed on the Main Market, and SumiSaujana Group Bhd, Elsa Bhd, GTA Holdings Bhd and United Asiapac Energy Bhd, which were listed on the ACE Market. “The Bumiputera Economic Transformation Plan 2035 complements this direction by advancing meaningful Bumiputera participation, ownership and competitiveness.

items.title: Pahang puts RM450,000 into hunt for invasive redtail catfish threatening native fish
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Nov 21 — The Pahang government has allocated RM450,000 for a programme to control the redtail catfish population, which has been identified as a potential threat to the state’s native fish population if left unchecked. Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the programme, being carried out simultaneously at seven locations statewide, including Pekan and Jerantut as well as Temerloh, was aimed at reducing the population of the invasive fish species. He said the redtail catfish was a predatory alien species that could threaten the survival of other native fish species sharing the same habitat.

items.title: National health fund, cheaper insurance by 2027: Economy Ministry’s healthcare reform wish list
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The Ministry of Economy has outlined four strategic priorities to support the healthcare reform agenda under the 13th Malaysia Plan, focusing on healthcare investment, financing sustainability, industry and talent development. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the priorities would complement the Health Ministry’s role through national development planning, resource prioritisation and cross-sectoral coordination. He said the first priority was aligning healthcare investments with population needs, taking into account access to services, avoidable delays, workforce availability and operational resources.

items.title: Two vehicles, one viral cable heist: KL police on the hunt for daring thieves outside TREC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The police are actively tracking down a group of individuals suspected of stealing cables in front of the TREC premises on Jalan Tun Razak here, after the incident was recorded and went viral on social media today. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said his team received a report regarding a 38-second video uploaded on the Threads platform at around 9.50 am today. He said the incident that occurred during the day involved a group of individuals using two vehicles while cutting cables at the location.

items.title: Sejingkat Bridge won’t shut Pending Port, Sarawak deputy premier tells DAP critics
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 21 — Caretaker Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas has hit out at the Democratic Action Party (DAP) over its criticism of the Sejingkat Bridge, dismissing claims that the project would force Pending Port to close and cause job losses as malicious allegations. He said the criticism failed to take into account the Sarawak government’s wider plans for port infrastructure, recalling how opposition figures had gone to the opposite riverbank to record videos criticising the project. “They sarcastically claimed that the Sarawak government had made a mistake in constructing this bridge because Pending Port would close and people would lose their jobs.

items.title: ‘Sarawakians are smart’: Abang Johari welcomes BN, PAS decision to skip Sarawak polls
items.summary: The Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman said Sarawakians were well capable of looking after their own state and that outsiders should not interfere in its affairs. He also mentioned that Sarawak had acquired Bintulu Port for RM1.8 billion and set up a state-owned oil company, Petroleum Sarawak Berhad. We develop Sarawak and Sarawak will continue to progress and prosper.”

items.title: Fadillah: Sarawak should maximise its rights through negotiation, not by undermining Federation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof has reminded Sarawak that its pursuit of state rights must not come at the expense of the Federation, but should instead strike a balance between the interests of both sides. He said the best approach was to maximise the rights that Sarawak was entitled to through negotiations and cooperation with the Federal Government. Meanwhile, he said AOK had replaced ‘Lan Berambeh Anak Sarawak’ in Kuala Lumpur this year due to a packed schedule of events in Sarawak in November and December.

items.title: Ismail Lasim’s palace pledge vindicates us, Negeri Sembilan Pakatan says, urging BN and Perikatan to retract claims
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 21 — Negeri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan (PHNS) has described Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s stance on defending the royal institution and complying with decisions concerning the state’s customs and Constitution as being in line with the principles upheld by the coalition since the crisis erupted in the state. The state PH Leadership Council said the stance should provide an opportunity for the public to reassess various allegations levelled against the coalition during the recent Negeri Sembilan State Election campaign, including claims that it had interfered in customary affairs, influenced the palace and threatened the position of Islam. “Hence, the state PH demands that the leaderships of Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) retract those baseless allegations.

items.title: UKM logo to ride on Pocket Rocketman Azizulhasni’s jersey all the way to LA 2028
items.summary: UKM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Sufian Jusoh said the strategic partnership would see Azizulhasni appointed as UKM Global Ambassador, with the university also planning to become the main sponsor of the cyclist, popularly known as The Pocket Rocketman, until the Olympic Games. He said Azizulhasni was chosen not only for his sporting achievements but also for his international influence and reputation, which could help introduce UKM to the global community. “We want to bring UKM’s good name to the global stage.

items.title: Promised quick gold returns, Terengganu retiree pays out RM131,820 before smelling a rat
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Nov 21 — A retiree lost RM131,820 after falling victim to an online investment scam. Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 59-year-old woman joined a gold investment scheme advertised on Facebook on October 30. He said the victim, who communicated with a male suspect via WhatsApp, invested her retirement savings after being promised lucrative returns within a short period.

items.title: Paralympian, hockey forward and sprinters among Perak honours for Sultan’s 70th birthday
items.summary: Also in attendance were Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah. Universiti Teknologi Petronas deputy vice-chancellor Prof Dr Abd Rashid Abd Aziz, National Registration Department (Management) deputy director-general Raja Azlal Raja Azman and Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris deputy vice-chancellor Prof Dr Raja Nor Safinas Raja Harun were among 11 recipients of the Darjah Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini. Sultan Nazrin also conferred the Darjah Paduka Mahkota Perak (PMP) on 31 recipients, including Perak and Kedah Orang Asli Development Department director Hairulnizam Abd Rahman and Perak Fire and Rescue Department deputy director Yusri Mohd Yusoff @ Hashim.

items.title: Penang CM Chow Kon Yeow promises answers on Perak water deal as Lim Guan Eng keeps up the heat
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 21 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today said he will hold a press conference in the next few days to explain the state’s RM24.6 billion water supply deal with Perak, after repeated criticism from DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng. Lim, the former chief minister and Air Putih assemblyman, has repeatedly raised the matter on social media. Chow also accused Lim of misleading the public despite repeated explanations.

items.title: Penang Umno-Pakatan pact must hold till end of term, says Chow Kon Yeow as PKR rep sounds alarm
items.summary: He was reacting to PKR’s Fahmi Zainol, the Pantai Jerejak assemblyman, who had questioned why DAP still keeps an Umno representative in the Penang government, several local news outlets reported. Chow, who is also Penang PH chairman, said state leaders could voice their views but the final say on cooperation with Umno rested with the PH central leadership. Asked whether Penang DAP would review its ties with Umno, Chow said that was a matter for the national leadership, The Star reported.

items.title: Azmin at Amanah convention: Delegates clap, Pakatan-Bersatu watchers take note
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 21 — Dressed in blue, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali walked into the Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) National Convention here this morning, and the hall took notice, Sinar Harian reported. The Malay-language daily said he arrived at Dewan Raja Muda Musa in Section 7 and was seen chatting warmly with Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu and deputy president Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa. PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun was also present.

items.title: Perak water or bust: PBAPP says Penang has run out of options after 98pc EGM vote
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 21 — Penang’s RM24.6 billion plan to buy treated water from Perak has won the backing of 98 per cent of shareholders in PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB), the parent company of the state water utility, at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) here today. Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) chief executive officer Datuk K. Pathmanathan said the state’s Water Contingency Plan 2030 had run out of options within Penang, The Star reported. Also present were PBAHB group chairman and Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, State Secretary Datuk Jafri Abdul Jalil and PBAHB chief financial officer Mary Ann Harris.

items.title: Not a specialist yet, so no specialist pay: Health DG explains on-call allowance row
items.summary: However, he said the MOH provides the Pre-Gazettement Specialist Incentive Payment to officers who meet the eligibility requirements, in recognition of their contributions throughout the SWE period. The clarification follows public concerns over Etap payments to medical officers undergoing SWE. Dr Mahathar said SWE is a mandatory period of supervised work experience under a medical specialist after an officer has completed specialist training, before being registered as a specialist in the National Specialist Register (NSR) under the Malaysian Medical Council.

items.title: Real test of China ties is how many Malaysian SMEs join global supply chains, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Kingfa, Plastech China and Eternal Asia are exploring opportunities to source supplies from Malaysia, covering speciality chemicals, polymers and palm-based products. Malaysian Investment Development Authority chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said foreign investments also open significant opportunities for Malaysian companies to become suppliers to global corporations. Tengku Zafrul said China recorded RM38.6 billion in approved investments in Malaysia during the first nine months of 2026.

items.title: Perak MB lauds MRCB for upgrading rural Lenggong school under Madani Adopted Schools programme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad has praised Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) for upgrading a rural school in Lenggong under the Madani Adopted Schools programme, Scoop reported. Saarani, a former teacher, visited SMK Dato’ Ahmad yesterday, where MRCB had refurbished the teachers’ room and digital room. SMK Dato’ Ahmad teacher Aziah Adam, who retires next month, thanked MRCB for the upgrade.

items.title: Report: LTAT board picks Achi Jaya as preferred buyer for BPlant, final nod rests with PM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) is expected to meet Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim soon to discuss the proposed sale of Boustead Plantations Bhd (BPlant) to Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd, Sinar Harian reported. Citing information it had obtained, the Malay daily said LTAT’s board of directors is believed to have already chosen Achi Jaya as its preferred buyer. However, the deal, which is reportedly worth about RM3.5 billion, still needs the prime minister’s final approval, the daily said.

items.title: Integrity can’t just be preached, it must be practised, says UKM chancellor Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: BANGI, Nov 21 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has called for integrity, transparency and accountability to be put into practice in every aspect of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia’s (UKM) administration to strengthen public confidence in the institution. His Royal Highness, who is also UKM chancellor, said integrity should not merely be a principle that is proclaimed, but must instead be reflected in the university’s financial management, administration and every decision it makes. Also present were Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, UKM pro-chancellor Tan Sri Datuk Rafiah Salim, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and UKM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Sufian Jusoh.

items.title: Tuhau, not tenderloin? Sabah wants a rethink of how poverty is measured
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 21 — Sabah’s Food Poverty Line Income (PGK) calculation method needs to be reviewed to ensure a more accurate measure of poverty that reflects local living conditions, culture and dietary habits, particularly in rural areas, said Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) Secretariat chief coordinating officer Datuk Datu Rosmadi Datu Sulai. He said the measurement method should take into account the unique characteristics of Sabah’s communities, whose dietary needs and practices differ from those in Peninsular Malaysia. He said these differences could affect the calculation of food costs and, consequently, the determination of the number of people living in poverty.

items.title: Perak school squeeze to ease with 844-seat SK Seri Chemor in 2032
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 21 — The planned construction of Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Seri Chemor near here has brought relief to local residents grappling with student overcrowding at primary schools around Chemor and Chepor. The father of two boys aged seven and three said the new school would ease his family’s daily routine because it is close to his mother-in-law’s house in Tanah Hitam, where his children stay before and after school. Kamalul Hayyat also intends to enrol his youngest son at SK Seri Chemor, noting the journey from his mother-in-law’s house to the school takes five minutes.

items.title: Two young children killed as fire destroys 90pc of house in Kedah village
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Two children, aged one year and four months and three years old, were found burnt on a bed after a fire broke out at a house in Kampung Teloi Tua, Sik, Kedah early this morning. Sinar Harian reported that firefighters from the Sik Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene at 6.27am, shortly after receiving an emergency call. “The firefighting operation used two hose streams, with water sourced from the fire engine’s tank and a fire hydrant.

items.title: Trailer runs red light, hits and drags teen motorcyclist at Kampar junction
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — A 19-year-old college student survived after a trailer hit his motorcycle and dragged it at a traffic light junction near a supermarket in Kampar, Perak yesterday. Kampar district police chief Superintendent Mohamad Nazri Daud told the Malay daily that the victim survived with injuries to his left leg. Mohamad Nazri said the trailer driver had been detained to assist investigations under Section 43 of the Road Transport Act 1987.

items.title: Kota Kinabalu stabbing: Sabah police nab suspected killer at Tawau jetty after six-day manhunt
items.summary: TAWAU, Nov 21 — Police arrested a 38-year-old man sought in connection with a fatal stabbing in Kuala Manggatal, Kota Kinabalu, at the Tawau Public Jetty around 11.30am on Friday. District police chief ACP Rosdi Mat Jusoh confirmed that the suspect, who had been wanted since Nov 15, was detained to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder. Rosdi urged the public not to speculate or spread unverified information that could compromise ongoing police investigations.

items.title: Pay RM900m before December sitting of state legislative assembly, Sabah Pakatan tells Putrajaya
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 21 — Sabah (PH) Pakatan Harapan wants the federal government to disburse the remaining RM900 million in interim payments for Sabah’s 40 per cent revenue entitlement before the State Legislative Assembly sitting next month. Sabah PH chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the interim payment had been increased to RM1.5 billion, comprising RM600 million that had already been gazetted and paid, while the remaining RM900 million was being processed. Mustapha said Sabah PH was also proposing that future interim payments be increased progressively each year, rather than remain at a fixed amount for five years.
